title: Ideas
meta: Topics for your next posts: what people almost find you for on Google, and gaps in what you publish.

gsc.title: Searches you almost rank for
gsc.intro: Last 28 days on Google and 90 on Bing (which has less traffic). You show up on the second page (average position 8–20) with real impressions: a new post, or a better one, can move them to the first. No AI cost.
gsc.notConfigured: Neither Search Console nor Bing Webmaster is set up
gsc.notConfiguredBody: Set up Google Search Console or Bing Webmaster Tools (or both) to see these searches.
gsc.error: Could not read the search data: {error}
gsc.none: No searches on the second page
gsc.noneBody: With more impressions (or more time) they will show up here.
gsc.improveHint: This post already ranks: expand it in Ghost or write a more specific one.
gsc.topicFromQuery: A post that properly answers the search “{query}”: what people want to know when they search it, with concrete examples.
gsc.footnote: Data lags 2–3 days (Bing aggregates it by week). When a search shows up in both, impressions are added up. The table is kept until you press “Refresh”.

scanned.line: Checked: {parts}; none at average position 8–20 with 10 or more impressions.

ai.title: AI ideas
ai.intro: From your published posts and your drafts: follow-ups, missing how-tos, updates of old posts.
ai.introGsc: From your published posts, your drafts and the Google and Bing searches below.
ai.emptyBody: Press “Generate ideas”. It is a short AI call (cents) and counts towards spend and the daily cap.
ai.dismissedHint: Dismissed ideas are not proposed again when generating new ones.

ctr.title: Good position, few clicks
ctr.intro: Google searches where you already show up on the first page (position 1–7) but get less than half the usual clicks for that spot. The post ranks well: what doesn't convince is the title or meta description shown on Google. Change them in Ghost.
ctr.noneBody: Your first-page posts have a normal CTR for their position (or there are fewer than 50 impressions yet).
ctr.footnote: Google only (Bing gives no page). The “usual” CTR is a rough average from public studies: it varies a lot per search (if Google shows the answer directly, hardly anyone clicks).
